findings.finding: Peru's El Nino forecast has hardened since Credicorp last spoke on 2026-08-13. In July ENFEN saw 'strong' as most likely, with a 33% chance of 'extraordinary'. ENFEN Comunicado 18-2026 (16 Oct 2026, cited in DU 015-2026) now keeps coastal El Nino at EXTRAORDINARY magnitude through January 2027, and the central Pacific very strong to February 2027. At 2Q management booked only S/106m (27 bps of CoR) of El Nino overlay 'based on currently available information' and said it would reassess expected losses around end-3Q/early-4Q. A further overlay in 3Q, and a cautious 2027 cost-of-risk tone at Mibanco (2Q CoR 5.1%), are therefore likely. Management also said FY26 CoR stays inside 1.7-2.1% even under a severe scenario.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline history is untrustworthy (monthly 6-Ks, not prints). From confirmed releases: 2Q26 (with the first El Nino overlay and CoR at 1.9%) drew a modest reaction, about +0.8% per an undated aggregator. 4Q25, an EPS miss, fell about 2.4% the next session. Provision surprises at this name have historically moved it low single digits.
findings.why_not_priced: The El Nino path is public and well covered, and the 20-day -6.4% may already hold part of it. What is not public is the size of the 3Q overlay. If the market had fully priced a large additional overlay, consensus EPS would sit below 2Q's ~$7.3-7.4. It sits higher, at $7.51-7.55.
findings.independence: Credicorp's own 2Q release states the reassessment timing and the S/106m/27bps overlay (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001001290/000114036126033379/ef20080305_ex99-1.htm). The ENFEN escalation path is also covered by El Buho/Gestion/Infobae (https://www.infobae.com/peru/2026/07/18/enfen-alerta-de-un-fenomeno-de-el-nino-de-magnitud-extraordinaria-hacia-finales-de-2026-en-peru/). This is weather-to-bank transmission that the company has not quantified.

findings.finding: Credicorp's 2Q26 6-K shows 1H26 ROE of 21.2% (2Q 20.3%) against a FY2026 guide of 'around 19.5%, with a current bias to the upside'. 2Q also lifted loan growth to ~12%, fee growth to high teens and the medium-term ROE target to ~22%. Holding the 19.5% guide would require 2H ROE near 18%. A 3Q around 20% therefore makes it likely the FY ROE guide is formally raised or firmed at or above 20% on the 3Q release or call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2Q26, where the ROE guide was reaffirmed with an upside bias and the medium-term target raised to 22%, drew a muted reaction (~+0.8%, undated aggregator). 2Q25, a beat, gained +0.71% (https://ng.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-credicorp-beats-q2-2025-forecasts-stock-rises-93CH-2067234). This name does not pay much for beats or reaffirmations.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: consensus at $7.51-7.55 is already above 2Q actual, so the street models 2H at the 1H run-rate rather than at the 19.5% guide. What remains is a formal raise. Against that, the Strategic Update on Nov 17 (outside the window) gives management a reason to hold the guide until then.
findings.independence: Quartr's 2Q26 summary records the same raised loan and fee guide (https://quartr.com/events/credicorp-ltd-bap-q2-2026_Fk4RVchn). Same company document family, so this is not independent evidence on the number.

findings.finding: Peruvian private credit grew 10.3% YoY in September 2026 (BCRP data via Caretas, published 2 Nov). That is unchanged from August and up from 8.7% in June, with lending to individuals accelerating to 11.0% (consumer-led) and dollar credit +14.1%. This supports the volume and NII line for BCP and Mibanco in 3Q and sits inside Credicorp's raised ~12% loan-growth guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loan-growth beats have not been rewarded much at this name (2Q26 13.1% YoY loans with the guide raised to ~12%; reaction ~+0.8%).
findings.why_not_priced: System data are public. Already inside the company's guided range, so mostly priced. This is a system proxy, not BCP's own number.
findings.independence: Infomercado reports the August 10.3% acceleration (https://infomercado.pe/credito-al-sector-privado-se-acelera-y-crece-10-3-en-agosto/). Proxy only.

findings.finding: Decreto de Urgencia 015-2026 (El Peruano, 31 Oct 2026) authorises up to S/2bn of CRECER fund guarantees covering 70-95% of new and reprogrammed MYPE soles loans in El Nino emergency departments. It allows reprogramming of up to 36 months with up to 12 months' grace, eligible only for borrowers classified Normal/CPP at 31 Aug 2026. This lowers loss-given-default on Mibanco's and BCP's most El Nino-exposed micro and SME book, and gives management a mitigant to cite on the call alongside any overlay.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance found for this name. Past state guarantee schemes (Reactiva/Impulso MyPeru) were folded into the provisioning narrative rather than traded on alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Published nine days before the print in the official gazette and not covered in English wires found. Its effect on Credicorp's expected-loss model is not quantified anywhere, and the call is the first place it can be.
findings.independence: Shares the document with the El Nino finding, which uses it for the ENFEN date. This finding uses the guarantee terms, a different part. Policy transmission is unconfirmed by the company.

findings.finding: The BCRP held its reference rate at 4.25% at its October 2026 meeting, a 13th straight hold, while 9 of 13 Bloomberg-surveyed analysts expected a hike. September inflation was 4.5%, above the 1-3% target. Funding costs in 3Q were therefore stable, consistent with the 2Q statement that NIM is trending to the high end of guidance. A hike signalled for the near term is a mild forward NIM tailwind for a deposit-rich bank.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history found for rate decisions specifically.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and macro. The sign of its effect on Credicorp's NIM guide is ambiguous, so it is sized at zero.
findings.independence: Peru Retail, 9 Oct 2026, reports the same hold (https://www.peru-retail.com/bcrp-mantiene-la-tasa-de-referencia-en-425-por-mas-de-un-ano-que-factores-influyen-en-su-decision/).

findings.finding: This is the first earnings call with a new CFO. Ignacio Belaunde became CFO of Credicorp and BCP on 1 Oct 2026, and the prior CFO Alejandro Perez-Reyes moved to run Mibanco and microfinance, replacing Javier Ichazo. Both were announced 13 May 2026. A new CFO one week before a Strategic Update tends toward conservative framing of guidance on the 3Q call.
findings.why_not_priced: Announced six months ago, so priced as a fact. Its only relevance is tone on the call.

outside_window.finding: Credicorp hosts its 2026 Strategic Update on 17 Nov 2026 ('maturity, monetization and operating leverage', AI and technology). New medium-term targets, capital return and Yape monetisation targets are more likely to land there than on the 10 Nov call.

Management's 2Q release says the strongest El Nino credit effects could materialise in early 2027, particularly 1Q27. The loss itself lands after this window. Only the 3Q overlay and tone land inside it, and those are filed above.

lessons_applied: Rule 5 (documents beat inference; weather-to-bank transmission is a proxy) plus rule 6 (inside the guide: management said FY CoR stays in 1.7-2.1% even under a severe scenario): El Nino overlay finding shrunk from -1.0 to -0.6.
Rule 6 (inside the guided range): the credit-growth proxy sits inside the ~12% loan guide, cut from +0.4 to +0.2.

Rule 1 (the reaction function vetoes; this name pays little for beats or reaffirmations, ~+0.7-0.8% on recent beats): guidance finding cut from +0.6 to +0.5, and print_vs_bar lowered from +1.0 to +0.5 because a 3Q overlay can absorb operating strength.
Rule 5: the DU 015-2026 policy-transmission finding cut from +0.2 to +0.15.

Base-rate lesson (untrustworthy FPI history): abs_move set from confirmed releases (~1-2.5% realised) blended with the indicative 6.47% implied move, at 3.5, not from the baseline's 2.88% median, which includes non-earnings events such as the election runoff.
